newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: POLITICIANS SPREAD BLAME FOR DELAYING REPUBLIC CONVENTION
The Federal Government and Opposition are blaming each other today for delaying the Constitutional Convention until at least next year.
The Government is refusing to accept a Senate vote rejecting a voluntary poll to elect half the delegates to the Convention.
Parliamentary Secretary to the Prime Minister Nick Minchin says the government will wait three months and return its bill to the Senate.
That means the Convention can't be held before March, even if the Senate backs down on its demand for a compulsory poll.
Mr Minchin says Labor is obsessed with having a republic but has acted to prevent the Government advancing the debate by holding the December Convention it was elected to hold

But Opposition Leader Kim Beazley says the Government is to blame because it wants a poll which excludes millions of voters. "They are gutting their own convention, we're trying to put a body on it," Mr Beazley said.
MELBOURNE COULD STAGE FIRST EVENT OF SYDNEY OLYMPICS
Melbourne could stage the first event of the Sydney 2000 Olympics.
The Victorian Government says it would be a real coup to hold a soccer game two days before the opening ceremony.

The Victorian Sport Minister, Tom Reynolds, says he's awaiting official word, but understands soccer's organising body, FIFA, wants some games held before the Olympics opening to ease pressure on the hectic timetable.
It's believed soccer rounds would begin in Melbourne, Adelaide, Brisbane and Canberra, before any events start in Sydney.
Mr Reynolds says Victoria would welcome the opportunity to help make the Olympics a success for Australia, and showcase the state before the focus turns to Sydney.
In Sydney, Shadow Olympics Minister Ian Armstrong says it's reasonable for the first contests of the Olympics to be held in other cities before the opening ceremony.
While Mr Reynolds says the announcement is, a "real coup", Mr Armstrong says Sydney hasn't been upstaged.
APPEAL OVER AFP MURDER DISMISSED
The man convicted of the 1989 murder of Australian Federal Police Assistant Commissioner Colin Winchester, has had his appeal dismissed by the Federal Court.
In a judgement handed down this morning the full bench found David Harold Eastman failed to substantiate his grounds for appeal.
Former A.F.P Commander Rick Ninnes who led the inquiry into Mr Winchester's death says his investigation which had been questioned by Eastman during the appeal, was justified.
Mr Ninnes says the case has gone before a judge and jury and then before three judges, who have upheld Eastman's conviction.
AUST WON'T BOW TO INTERNATIONAL PRESSURE ON GREENHOUSE
The Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, says Australia won't bow to international pressure to reduce its Greehouse gas emissions.
His stand follows calls from Britain for developed countries to reduce greehouse gas emmissions by 15 per cent by the year 2010.
Mr Fischer says Australia won't be forced to tow the line.
"I'm not going to close down half the coal industry of Central Queensland, half the industry of the Hunter valley," he said.
Mr Fischer said the Government was batting for sensible, achieveable Greenhouse targets and not the "uniform fixed absolutism" that some were prosecuting elsewhere.
He said Australia was not alone in its stand against uniform emission targets.
He said the US Congress and Norway would not "jump to the tune" of uniform targets and Australia was gradually building a range of allies on the issue.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
